expectations.text: B1: Gives a concrete approach for macOS without installing anything
expectations.evidence: Concrete macOS approaches, nothing to install: 'on macOS use DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES or call the allocator directly'; 'Alternative simpler approach: call the allocator directly (link your malloc into the test program, rename or #define malloc to my_malloc). This is the most reliable on macOS'; plus DYLD_INTERPOSE macro code and a clang-built scratch test rig.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Reply does not end with a checkpoint; it cuts off mid-sentence: 'Common trick: use a static bootstrap b'. Checkpoint appears only as intent ('every reply ends with the checkpoint (command + expected output)') and plan item '(f) checkpoint command + expected output', never delivered at the end.

expectations.text: B3: Mentions DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES on macOS (vs LD_PRELOAD on Linux) or calling the allocator directly in tests
expectations.evidence: 'LD_PRELOAD is Linux-only; on macOS use DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES or call the allocator directly'; 'DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES is the macOS equivalent of LD_PRELOAD'; also gives DYLD_INTERPOSE code and the direct-link option.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: No install commands run (only ls/sw_vers/clang/echo), but a shell command wrote outside the project dir: './scratch/prog > /tmp_out.txt 2> /tmp_err.txt' (root-level paths), which the rule counts as a B4 failure.
